issues.description: GIT_MERGE.md is not executable verbatim from a secondary worktree and needs a documented worktree variant. Step 2 mandates 'git add -A', which this run's dispatch explicitly forbids (files were staged by explicit name throughout). Step 9 mandates 'git checkout main' + 'git pull --ff-only origin main' + 'git branch -d', which is structurally impossible when local main is checked out in the sibling worktree; the equivalent used here was 'git fetch origin main --prune && git checkout --detach origin/main', which satisfies the protocol's intent (return to a clean, current base) without ever touching the local main ref. The protocol's acceptance criteria ('git branch --show-current is main') therefore cannot be met literally in a worktree. Same class of documented deviation ORCH already recorded for GIT_SETUP.md at Step 00 of this run.

GIT_MERGE.md step 5's conflict-handling branch has no guidance for the case that actually occurred here -- a SEMANTIC conflict where both sides edited the same function and the correct resolution is to merge the two implementations rather than pick either. Step 5b says only 'apply the correct resolution (preserve valid changes from both sides)', which is right in principle but gives an agent with limited judgement nothing mechanical to follow, contrary to core-directives.md's weak-model-tolerance constraint. Worth adding a worked example (this REQ-023/REQ-024 tenant_scoped_migrations/0 merge is a good one) and an explicit instruction to verify post-merge that neither side's contract changed -- the @spec byte-identity check used here.

Latent defect found ON origin/main and repaired by this merge rather than merely noted: REQ-024 (PR #77) registered its event_type_registry migration in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 in the bare {version, module} form, which this run had already proved defective -- Ecto.Migrator.load_migration!/1 requires Code.ensure_loaded?(module), but priv/repo/migrations/*.exs is never compiled (mix.exs elixirc_paths = ["lib"]), so replay_migrations/2 raises Ecto.MigrationError in any VM where the module is not already loaded. Between PR #77 merging and this PR merging, main carried that defect. It is fixed here by routing REQ-024's entry through REQ-023's manifest, and was confirmed fixed in a cold --no-start VM. Recorded so the window is visible in the audit trail rather than disappearing silently into a conflict resolution.
